Home/Controls/Controls reference

Controls reference

These tables show default keys. For reassigned actions, use the key shown in Settings > Controls > Key bindings. Menu navigation and native window shortcuts keep their physical keys.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 3 min, then look things up · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents

  2. Keys that change meaning
  3. Furniture, doors and home
  4. Every control
  5. How this was checked

The keys you will use most

Key or actionWhat it does
W / A / S / DWalk. Fly horizontally in creative flight.
MouseLook around, once you have clicked the world to capture the pointer.
SpaceJump; rise while flying or swimming.
ShiftSneak (ledge guard), dive, descend in flight or steady a ranged weapon.
Ctrl + WSprint.
Left click (hold)Mine or remove the block you aim at; hit an animal.
Right clickPlace the held block (a block selected, no tool equipped); hold to draw a bow or wind up a throw. Also uses what you aim at: a door, chest, seat, bed or lamp.
EOpen or close the inventory.
1 – 9, 0 / wheelChoose a hotbar slot.
TabEquip the next tool (inventory closed) or the next inventory tab (inventory open).
F4Switch between creative and survival.
R / T / XSurvival: eat, drink, quick-craft.
EscClose the active layer or open the pause menu.
F6Save now. In a server world you joined, nothing is saved on your computer and the game says so.
F10Save a screenshot.
Tip. Sprint and sneak use held keys by default; crawl is a toggle. Change Hold/Toggle in Settings > Gameplay > Movement. Keyboard, mouse and controller support

Change a gameplay key

  1. Open Settings > Controls > Key bindings.
  2. Select an action with Up/Down and press Enter, or click its row to start capture. Previous/Next or Page Up/Page Down changes action page.
  3. Press a physical key. Esc cancels capture; Delete leaves the action unbound.
  4. If a conflict appears, choose another key or change the other action: shared assignments can trigger both. Reset keys or Backspace outside capture restores every default binding.

Esc, F6, F11 and Print Screen are reserved. Native shortcuts such as Alt+Enter and Ctrl+Q, menu navigation and text entry keep their physical keys. Keyboard, mouse and controller support

Keys that change meaning

  • Shift is shared by default: sneak on the ground, dive in water, descend while flying, and steady a bow or rifle. Building detail has its own action. Sneaking (ledge guard)
  • Tab equips tools when the inventory is closed and switches tabs when it is open. Equipping tools (Tab cycling)
  • Z zooms, but Ctrl + Z is undo, so Z does not zoom while Ctrl is held. It undoes furniture and chest refinishing steps in either mode, and building and door moves in creative. Hold to zoom
  • C crawls on foot. In a boat, it cycles camera stations. Crawling
  • F toggles flight in creative; in survival it only shows 'Flight is available in creative mode'. Creative flight
  • F5 cycles first person, third person rear and third person front. The perspective is not saved. Camera perspectives (F5)
  • B cycles creative brushes, and in survival takes the Blueprint tool out. With a furniture plan out it puts the plan away instead, and it cancels a door move. Creative brushes (B)
Tip. Key names describe physical positions. On a non-QWERTY board, use those positions or reassign gameplay actions. Keyboard, mouse and controller support

Furniture, doors and home

Default keys. Survival needs a furniture hammer in your pack for plans; Creative does not. Furniture and carpentry and Storage, beds and lamps explain each step; doors are in Building basics.

While a furniture plan is selected

Key or actionWhat it does
E, with a plan or the hammer in handOpen the carpentry workbench. Aim at furniture first to change its woods, or at a placed chest to refinish it.
Right clickPlace the furniture at the ghost. With only the hammer in hand, it opens the workbench instead.
RTurn the ghost 90 degrees. Wall pieces: aim at a wall side and turn their back toward it.
Left clickTake up the aimed furniture. Empty its storage first.
Shift + Left clickLock the aimed furniture to move it. R turns it, right click places it, left click cancels.
Shift + Right clickJoin a floor kitchen piece to the side of the aimed one.
BPut the furniture away.
Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Shift + ZUndo / redo your last furniture step.

Using furniture (plan put away)

Key or actionWhat it does
Right click a seatSit. Space or right click stands you up when the way is clear.
Right click a bedLie down. Space or right click gets you up when the way is clear.
Right click a lampSwitch it on or off (no tool or plan in hand).
Right click a chest or storage furnitureOpen its storage. Click an item to move one; Shift + click moves as many of that item as fit.
Right click a cooking stoveOpen its panel. Click moves one item, Shift + click as many as fit; Start cooks one batch.
Right click a table top, red lantern selectedPut the lantern on display. Works on tables, desks, bookcases and wall shelves. Ctrl + Z undoes it.
Right click the display, empty slot selectedTake the lantern back.

Doors

Key or actionWhat it does
Right click a doorOpen or close it.
Middle click a door (Creative)Copy its exact style, wood and size into your hand.
Shift + Left click a closed door (Creative)Lock it to move. R turns it, right click places it, left click or B cancels. Ctrl + Z and Ctrl + Shift + Z undo and redo the move.

Home tab

Key or actionWhat it does
Arrow keys, Page Up / Page DownMove between the actions and the carried and stored lists.
Enter or SpaceUse the selected action, or move the selected item. Shift moves as many as fit.
Good to know. With a block or empty hands, aiming at furniture refuses mining ("Furniture blocks that mining target") and block placement ("Furniture blocks that placement"). On a server, wait for the server to confirm before the next furniture, bed, stove or door-move action.

Each row names the feature that owns it; follow the link for its summary and source evidence. Rows for developer tools or features still in development carry a status label.
